display_name: DOJ/FTC Antitrust Guidelines for Business Activities Affecting Workers (2025): the Overview's list, the general principles and sections 1 to 7, as the sentences of the text that apply to an agreement, an exchange of information, an employment term or an earnings claim. Agency enforcement policy, not law.
seat: a business, or its counsel, asking what the guidelines say of an agreement with another business about workers, an exchange of information about workers, a term in its own employment contracts, or a claim it makes about workers' earnings

expected_failed_independent.why: Genuine ambiguities, left failing on purpose: each turns on a reading the text does not settle, and the fork register keeps both readings (line 511, F6; 552 and 553, F5; 669, F28; 735 and 736, F20). NOTES.md section 15 classifies all eleven failures of the independent pass.

scope: AGENCY ENFORCEMENT POLICY, NOT LAW (n.1: it 'has no force or effect of law'): every result is a sentence of the text, with its own modal and speaker; a sentence the text states flatly is reported as what the agencies state; no result says that conduct is lawful or unlawful. Each report is a LIST of the sentences that apply, in the text's order: EMPTY when none applies on the facts given (never a finding of lawfulness), NOTHING when the answer turns on a finding not made, or the case is one the section does not speak of (potential competitors in sections 2, 3 and 6; the same business named twice) (F23). Encoded: the Overview's list of five items and 'This list is not exhaustive' (an unnamed practice answers NOTHING, F3); the general principles (the agreement as a three-valued caller finding, F2; its form, never read; the kinds of evidence, reported, never weighed; whether the businesses compete for workers, from the labor markets each names compared ignoring case and surrounding whitespace, and a three-valued finding of potential competition, F1; every statement the text makes on whether an identified agreement's effects matter, with no precedence, F20); section 1 (the substance of wage-fixing and no-poach agreements, n.11; the crime and civil sentences for businesses that compete for workers and the 'illegal even if' and DOJ sentences for competing or potentially competing employers, F4; n.15 in place of 'illegal even if' on both its conjuncts, F5; the starting point, F6; the Criminal Antitrust Anti-Retaliation Act sentence, F21); section 2 (franchisor and franchisee, the per se sentence when they compete for workers, F7; the franchisor organizing among franchisees that compete, F9; franchisees among themselves, with the Overview's sentence on them, F24, F28); section 3 (exchanges with businesses that compete for workers, F13; the effect sentence on a three-valued finding, F12; through a third party, F25); section 4 (non-compete clauses, F14, F18, F26); section 5 (non-disclosure, training repayment, non-solicitation, exit fee or liquidated damages provisions and the unnamed rest, F16, F17, F27, F28); section 6 (the Overview's sentence on independent contractors and the competing platforms, F11); section 7 (false or misleading earnings claims, F19). Inputs, never computed: every finding (the agreement, potential competition, n.15's conjuncts (each three-valued), the exchange's effect, whether a term limits competition, impedes mobility or prevents the worker from leaving, whether a claim is false or misleading) and the labor markets. Not encoded: the FTC's 2024 non-compete rule and its litigation (dated, n.30-n.32), statutes and other agencies' authorities in the footnotes, section 8. No numeric inputs.

forks.F1: two businesses compete for workers when they name a labor market the same way, ignoring case and the whitespace around a name (one shared among several is enough); products and any collaborative relationship are not read; failing that, the caller's three-valued finding of potential competition (made: potentially competing; contrary: they do not compete, if both name their labor markets); NOTHING when, with no shared labor market, that finding is not made, or it is contrary and either business names none; NOTHING too when the two are the same business
forks.F2: the agreement is the caller's finding with three values (identified, found none, not determined), never inferred from the evidence, which is only reported
forks.F3: non-exhaustive lists: an Overview practice the list does not name answers NOTHING; other evidence is reported as such; an agreement of a type no section speaks of gets NOTHING from the effects question
forks.F4: section 1's crime and civil sentences (its first paragraph in the PDF) reach businesses that compete for workers; its 'illegal even if' sentence and the DOJ sentence, a paragraph of its own whose 'these agreements' is read with the preceding paragraph's, reach competing or potentially competing employers
forks.F5: n.15 needs both its conjuncts made and replaces only the 'illegal even if' sentence; a contrary finding on either leaves that sentence; otherwise NOTHING; it does not reach the crime, civil or DOJ sentences (the independent author reads it otherwise), section 2 or section 6; the general principles' collaborative relationship is not one of its conjuncts
forks.F6: the starting point gets only 'may be a form of wage fixing under the law', not 'illegal even if' (the independent author reads it as wage fixing); the effects question and section 6 give NOTHING for it
forks.F7: section 2's per se sentence for a franchisor and its franchisee needs them to compete for workers (changed on review at the parent session's direction); not competing: the scrutiny sentence only; potentially competing or not stated: NOTHING; the alternative, version 0.1.0's, is unconditioned
forks.F9: section 2's 'franchisees that compete for workers' means actual competitors, and the franchisor's sentence also needs its organizing or enforcing; potentially competing franchisees with the franchisor organizing: NOTHING
forks.F10: sections 1 and 2 do not read the kind of workers (6: workers include independent contractors)
forks.F11: section 6's 'competing platforms' compete for those workers in the same labor market; potentially competing platforms, and a starting point, NOTHING; the Overview's sentence on independent contractors has no condition on competing
forks.F12: section 3's effect finding has three values: found (the sentence), contrary found (no effect sentence), not assessed (for competitively sensitive information between competitors, the whole answer NOTHING, as F23 has it); intent is not read
forks.F13: section 3 reads only businesses that compete for workers in the same labor market (EMPTY for non-competitors; NOTHING for potential competitors, of whom it does not speak, and when not stated), because its heading and first two sentences say 'with competitors'; only the sentences that say 'competitively sensitive', and the conspiracy sentence with them, need that field
forks.F14: 'that limit competition' (4) and 'that impede worker mobility or otherwise undermine competition' (5) are conditions
forks.F15: the kind of term is the caller's (a penalty on leaving is a non-compete provision in Overview item 4 and an exit fee in section 5)
forks.F16: one 'function to prevent' finding for section 5's four bullets; for training repayment, non-solicitation and exit fees the 'depending on the facts and circumstances' sentence is unconditional and 'such as if' is an example given beside it (three independent expectations corrected as test-author errors); for a non-disclosure agreement 'when' is a condition
forks.F17: 'Such provisions raise many of the same antitrust concerns' reaches the kinds section 5 names (a non-disclosure agreement only when broad, F27); 'may investigate if there are indications that such a restrictive condition' reaches every kind, the unnamed one included, on its finding
forks.F18: section 4 covers non-compete clauses and section 5 every other kind; neither reads the other's findings
forks.F19: the Overview's 'false claims' sentence needs a false claim; the body's 'may investigate' sentence takes false or misleading
forks.F20: every statement on whether the effects matter that applies is listed, with no precedence among sections; section 1's crime and DOJ sentences are given to a franchisor and franchisee that compete for workers (the independent author reads section 2 as taking them away)
forks.F21: the Criminal Antitrust Anti-Retaliation Act sentence for the four roles it names reporting an antitrust crime; NOTHING otherwise; the Act itself is not encoded
forks.F22: the caller names the Overview item; the facts are read in sections 1 to 5
forks.F23: EMPTY: no sentence of the section applies on the facts given; NOTHING: the answer turns on a finding not made, the case is one the section does not speak of, or the text does not answer; one open sentence makes the whole report NOTHING; neither is a finding of lawfulness
forks.F24: 'No-poach clauses in franchise agreements are also subject to antitrust scrutiny' is read for a franchisor and its franchisee; franchisees among themselves get Overview item 2's sentence, which names them, listed first
forks.F25: section 3's sentence on providing information 'through an algorithm or through a third party's tool or product' is read for any route through a third party
forks.F26: section 4's 'Non-compete clauses that restrict workers from switching jobs or starting a competing business can violate the antitrust laws' is read as a condition (either finding); the alternative reads it as describing every non-compete
forks.F27: section 5's 'Such provisions' includes a non-disclosure agreement only when it functions to prevent leaving or reaches any information usable in or relating to an industry (Overview item 5: 'overly broad non-disclosure agreements')
forks.F28: the other-law sentences of sections 2 and 5 ('may violate other federal and state laws'; 'State law also sets limits on training repayment requirements and NDA restrictions') are said of the kinds they name without condition (the independent author reads the second as not said of a narrow non-disclosure agreement)

not_reviewed.note: No domain expert has read this against the guidelines. An independent test pass and an adversarial review, both by other agents, were answered in version 0.2.0 (NOTES.md sections 15 and 16); neither is a domain expert's review. Every fork is assumed, not ruled (NOTES.md section 8).
